These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Basavaraja, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Both these appeals arise out of judgment and award dated 13th November, 2017 passed in ECA No.25 of 2016 passed by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner under Employees'
Compensation Act, Belagavi (for brevity, hereinafter referred to as the "Commissioner ECA")
2.
For the sake of convenience, parties in these appeals are referred to as per their status and rank before the Commissioner ECA.

Brief facts of the petition filed under Section 3 read with Section 22 of Employees (Workmen's)
Compensation Act, 1923 read with amended Act of 1995 and 2000 is that, on 10th January, 2016 at about 1.30 pm, petitioner was plying autorickshaw of respondent No.1 to Desur village, Belagavi Taluk, on Belagavi-Khanapur Road, the said autorickshaw turtled and the claimant sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to hospital and was there as an inpatient and was Shri.
Krishna S/O Yankappa Rathod vs Shri.

Jafarsadiq S/O Qasimasab on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148717981/
3 operated for fractures and spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses.
The said accident occurred due to and in the course of employment with Respondent No.1.
It is contended that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 25 years and was hale and healthy and was earning Rs.300/- per day.
Because of the accident, petitioner is not earning anything.

On all these grounds,
sought for awarding compensation.
4. Upon service of summons, Respondent No.1 appeared and filed his statement of objections contending that the petitioner was driver working under him.

During and in the course of employment, the petitioner suffered injuries and the same were within his knowledge and further contended that the autorickshaw is insured with respondent No.2.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8930-DB 5.

The substance of statement of objections of respondent No.2 is that, the petitioner was unauthorised driver of autorickshaw and the respondent No.1 has entrusted the vehicle to the driver who was not having valid driving licence.
The driver was having licence to ride motorcycle with gear from 05th February, 2014 to 04th February, 2034.
Regional Transport Officer, Belagavi has issued licence authorising him to drive Light Motor Vehicle (NT) till 04th February, 2034.
Thus, the driver was not authorised to drive passenger autorickshaw.
Further denying all other averments made in the claim petition, sought for dismissal of claim petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, the Commissioner ECA framed issues as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he is employee within the meaning of Employees Compensation Act?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that the accident has arisen out of and during the course of employment?
3. What was the age and income?
4. What order?
To prove the case of the petitioner, two witnesses were examined as PWs1 and 2 and marked twelve documents as Exhibits P1 to P12.
On closure of petitioner's side evidence, respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW1 and two documents were marked as Exhibits R1 and R2.

sentences.text: Issue No.3:
The petitioner is aged 25 years and earning Rs.7,500/- per month Issue No.4:
As per final order 8.

In view of the above finding, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.10,94,942/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum payable after thirty days from the date of accident, till deposit.

Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award passed by the Commissioner ECA the claimant has preferred MFA No.102592 of 2018, seeking enhancement of compensation; and United India Insurance Company has preferred MFA No.101026 of 2018, questioning quantum and also liability of compensation.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8930-DB 9.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant- Insurance Company submits that the judgment and award passed by the Commissioner ECA, is contrary to law and material on record.

The Commissioner ECA has totally erred in holding that the claimant has sustained injuries arising during and in the course of employment, whereas the vehicle is a passenger carrying autorickshaw and accordingly, he submits that the petition by tortfeaser without following the law laid down by the Division Bench of this Court in the case of LOUIS v. MARTIN KARORA AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2010 KAR. 2006, is not maintainable.

entities.text: LOUIS v. MARTIN KARORA AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2010 KAR. 2006
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the Commissioner ECA has utterly erred in fastening liability on the appellant-Insurance in spite of the claimant holding licence to drive Light Motor Vehicle (NT) and the vehicle involved in the accident was a passenger autorickshaw.
Hence, he submits that the Tribunal ought to have exonerated the appellant from the liability of paying compensation to the claimant.

He further submits that Commissioner, ECA has totally erred in reckoning the wages of claimant at Rs.7,500/- per month without there being no documentary evidence and the Commissioner has totally erred in assessing disability of the claimant at 100% based on the NC: 2023:KHC-D:8930-DB evidence of PW2 who is a non-treated doctor for the fracture of mild wedging of D12 vertebra allegedly leading to paraplegia.
On all these grounds sought for allowing the appeal.

10. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the claimant at Rs.7,500/- per month though there is oral and documentary evidence to show that the claimant was getting salary of Rs.300/- per day.

The Commissioner, ECA is not justified while assessing the loss of earning capacity of the petitioner to the extent of 60% which is against the evidence of PW2 Doctor who has assessed the loss of earning capacity to the extent of 100% to the whole body and provisions of Section 4(1)(c)(ii) of the Employees Compensation Act.

11. These appeals were admitted to consider the following substantial questions of law:
1. Whether the Commissioner under Employees' Compensation Act has awarded the compensation in accordance with law and facts 2.
What Order?

Regarding Point No.1:
13.

With regard to liability of insurance is concerned, the Commissioner, ECA, at paragraph 14 and 15 of the judgment, has observed as under:
"14.

R.w.1 is the authorized officer of Insurance Company, who has stated that as per driving license at Exh.p.10, the petitioner was permitted to drive the motor cycle with gear from 5.2.2017 to 4.2.2034 and he was authorized to drive LMV (NT) till 4.2.2034,hence, the respondent no.1 knowingly entrusted the vehicle to the unauthorized person not having valid driving license.

The same line of arguments are also advanced by the learned counsel for the respondent no.2.
15.
Now to consider the validity of the driving license, whether there is breach of policy or not.

Exh.p.10 is the driving license, it discloses that the petitioner was allowed to drive motor cycle with gear from 5.2.2014 onwards and not from 5.2.2017 as contended by R.w.1 and he was having authorization to drive LMV (NT) from 5.2.2014 till 4.2.2034 and as per the ruling of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company, disposed of on 3.7.2017

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has clarified and issued directions in - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8930-DB the matter pertaining to the driving licenses containing the endorsement as LMV (NT), hence the driving license of petitioner at Exh.P.10 is valid driving license."
14.

On careful examination of the evidence placed by both the parties and also relying upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Commissioner, ECA held that the petitioner was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, there is no force in the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company.

15. As regards compensation awarded by the Commissioner, ECA is concerned, the Commissioner has observed that the petitioner was aged 25 years as on the date of accident and he is suffering from paraplegia and the same has been taken judicial notice of.

The Commissioner has observed as under:
"The claimant is brought with a help of parents and was made to sit by them on stool and he is having drain for the purpose of urine, attached him."

6 16.

As regards disability of the petitioner, at paragraphs 20 to 23, it is observed as under:
"20. Petitioner is meagerly educated person and he knows only survives by driving and not skilled person.
There are no avenues for him for getting any other job or employment avenues.
The loss of sensation of lower limbs inability to lift on lower limbs and walk, inability to appreciate bowel and urinary bladder sensation has made him a vegetative body.
He has to rely upon someone for all his routine activities including thenature call.
Such condition of petitioner is nothing but total economical death.
Neither he can generate any income nor he can enjoy the life, nor can he expect any future enjoyments or hope of recovery.
For petitioner it is 100% loss of earning capacity.

21. It is held in a ruling reported in 2015 ACJ 236 (Karnataka) (Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Savithri Hudge and another), wherein, Hon'ble High Court considering the injury to the spine and fractures of vertebrae and compression of spinal cord and unable to lifting of both hands and loss of sensation of trunk, 100% disability was assessed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
22. It is also held in a decision reported in 2013 ACJ 1693 (Kalvi V/s. Murugesan and others), wherein, for the patient suffering from paraplegia, 100% disability is taken and also in a decision reported in 2013 ACJ 696 (Vijaykumar Babulal Modi V/s.
Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation), for the compression of L1, L2, L4 and T12, there is 100% disablement was considered.
23.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner is disable from earning anything.
The arguments of Insurance Company that the petitioner has not surrendered his license etc., cannot be the ground to presume that the petitioner is still capable of earning.
When the petitioner cannot move without the help of two, he going to the RTO office - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8930-DB and surrendering the license is remote act.
Hence, the petitioner is disabled to 100%.

Thus the  petitioner is entitled for compensation for loss of earning capacity as under :
7500 x 60% x 216.91 x 100% = Rs.9,76,095/-."

7 17.
But the Commissioner, ECA has committed an error in assessing the income of Rs.7,500/-.

In view of sub-Section 1(B) of Section 4 of Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the Commissioner ought to have assessed the income of the petitioner at Rs.8,000/- per month as per notification dated 31st May, 2010 issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, New Delhi.

sentences.text: Hence by taking the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.8,000/-, the loss of earning capacity comes to Rs.10,41,168/- (Rs.8,000/- x 60% x 216.91).

In the result, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:

 1. Loss of earning capacity 10,41,168.00  2. Medical Expenses 1,18,847.00  Total 11,60,015.00 18.
Since the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of accident, the respondent No.2-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, we answer point No.1 in the affirmative.
